title: Vanishing of higher direct images for retrocompact opens in local dimension at most one
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] such that every local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and has ring Krull dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be an open subset which is retrocompact, meaning that $U\cap V$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $V\subseteq X$ (quasi-compactness as in [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]). Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of the open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent] and every integer $p>0$, the higher direct image $R^pj_*\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-cohomology] is zero.

source.place: Tag 09N8, label lemma-affine, statement at lines 7747-7752; used in Tag 09N9, label lemma-open-in-affine-curve-affine

proof.text: To test vanishing of $R^p j_*\mathcal F$, it is enough to test its stalk at an arbitrary point $x\in X$. The map from $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}$ to $X$ is flat: on an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$, the stalk identification gives $\mathcal O_{X,x}\cong A_{\mathfrak p_x}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], and this localization is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. The inclusion $j$ is quasi-compact by retrocompactness and quasi-separated because its diagonal is an isomorphism. Therefore the flat base-change theorem [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] identifies the stalk calculation with the higher direct images of the pulled-back open $U_x\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}$.

source.place: Tag 09N8, proof: "We may check the vanishing ... at stalks" and the appeal to Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02KH (flat base change)

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and let $\mathfrak m$ be its closed point. The local-spectrum classification [lem-a1-local-spectrum-open-classification] applies because $A$ is Noetherian and has Krull dimension at most one. If $\mathfrak m\in U_x$, then $U_x=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the inclusion is the identity, whose higher direct images vanish. If $\mathfrak m\notin U_x$, then $U_x$ is an affine open with finite discrete underlying space.

source.place: Tag 09N8, proof: local spectrum case split at the closed point

proof.text: In the second case of Step 2, the morphism $U_x\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine because both source and target are affine. Applying the affine higher-direct-image theorem [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hi] to the quasi-coherent pullback of $\mathcal F$ gives $R^p(U_x\to\operatorname{Spec}A)_*\mathcal F_x=0$ for every $p>0$. Together with the identity case, this proves the vanishing of every stalk from Step 1, hence $R^p j_*\mathcal F=0$ for all $p>0$.
